title: The 5 phone accessories worth owning, ranked
dek: Built from six expert lists, then matched to real Lazada listings: a flight-friendly power bank, a fast charger, a cable that lasts, commute-ready earbuds and a tripod for trips.
teaser: Six expert lists, five picks: the accessories that make a phone easier to live with, ranked.
description: The phone accessories worth owning in the Philippines, ranked from six expert lists: power bank, fast charger, USB-C cable, noise-cancelling earbuds and a tripod, with pros, cons and sources.

hero.alt: AI sample render of a sunny condo desk with a sky-blue magnetic power bank on a phone, a pale blue cube charger, braided USB-C cables, black earbuds with their case and a black tripod holding a phone
hero.caption: AI sample render of our five picks, drawn from written descriptions of each product. The real product photos from Lazada are below.

intro: Your phone carries a lot of your day: payments, rides, work chats, the family group chat, maps and every photo from the last out-of-town trip. The accessories around it don't need to be fancy. They need to keep it charged, steady and easy to use, and they need to be genuine, because a fake charger or power bank isn't just money wasted. It can overheat.

So instead of starting from whatever sells, we started from the experts. We read six editorial accessory lists, counted what they agree on, set clear criteria for each item, and only then compared real listings against them.

curation.title: Six expert lists, one shortlist
summary: We read six editorial lists: Engadget, 9to5Google, SamMobile, CNET, How-To Geek and Unbox PH. The power bank is the only accessory all six include. Next come a case and a spare charging cable (five of six), then a wall charger and a stand, grip or mount (four of six).

We ranked the slots by how many lists include them, how often you would use them, and how much they matter here: long commutes, brownouts, flights and heat. Cases and car mounts are covered in the notes below instead of as picks.
steps: Read six editorial accessory lists and counted which accessory types they share.
Ranked the types by agreement, daily use and Philippine relevance, then set 3 to 4 checkable criteria per slot.
Compared 2 to 4 Lazada listings per slot on those criteria, price, seller and recent buyers.
Checked every product photo against its listing, and every power bank model code against Anker's 2025 recall list.
Dropped look-alike stores (we found fake "Anker" shops spelled with Greek and Cyrillic letters) and listings whose photos didn't match.

callouts.title: Flying soon? Know the power bank rules
callouts.body: CAAP bans power banks over 160Wh on flights, and up to 100Wh is allowed on board. Philippine Airlines and Cebu Pacific allow a maximum of two power banks of 100Wh or less. They must travel with you, not in checked bags, and both airlines say to keep them out of the overhead bin and not to charge with them during the flight. A 10,000mAh power bank is about 37Wh. Check your airline's latest rules before you fly.

sources.name: Unbox PH
CAPA
Cebu Pacific Help

callouts.title: Always check the model number
callouts.body: In June 2025, Anker recalled five power bank models (A1257, A1647, A1652, A1681 and A1689) because of battery cells from one supplier. Our pick, the A1685, is not one of them, and while researching we skipped a listing whose name still carries a recalled code. Whatever power bank you buy, make sure the model on the box matches the listing.

sources.name: 9to5Mac

callouts.title: Protect it first: case and screen protector
callouts.body: Cases and screen protectors are on most expert lists, but they have to match your exact phone model, so there is no single pick for everyone. Some phones sold here come with a basic clear case and a pre-applied screen film, so check the box first. If you buy one, choose the listing made for your model, ideally from the brand's own store.

sources.name: SamMobile
9to5Google

callouts.title: Why there is no car mount (yet)
callouts.body: Car mounts appear on three of the six lists, but none of the mounts we checked had an independent review we could verify, so we are holding off rather than guessing. If you use one, mount it low on the dashboard or an aircon vent, never in the middle of the windshield: the Anti-Distracted Driving Act (RA 10913) bans placements that block your view of the road.

sources.name: DriveSafe PH

sellerNote: Picks 1 to 4 are sold by the Anker Global store on Lazada. Anker Philippines' 18-month local warranty covers its official Philippine channels, so check the warranty and where the item ships from on the listing before you buy.

items.label: Best overall
items.name: Anker Zolo Magnetic Power Bank 10K (A1685)
items.verdict: Our top pick for keeping any USB-C phone going through a long commute or a full day out, plus magnetic charging for iPhones.
items.summary: If you buy only one accessory, make it a power bank. This Anker Zolo has its own USB-C cable built in, so you can top up on the bus, at the mall or during a brownout without hunting for a cord. iPhone owners get two extras: it snaps on magnetically, and it has a little stand for watching videos while it charges.

reviewers.point: Gave it an Editors' Choice. In their battery test it recharged an iPhone 16 Pro to 191%, the highest result they had recorded at the time.
The main catch: the built-in cable is USB-C, so it suits iPhone 15 and newer and USB-C Android phones, not older Lightning iPhones.
A1685 is not one of the five Anker power banks recalled in June 2025 (A1257, A1647, A1652, A1681, A1689).

pros: Built-in USB-C cable plus a spare USB-C port
Up to 30W wired, fast enough for iPhone 15+ and Android
Snaps onto MagSafe iPhones and has a kickstand
cons: Costs more than a basic 10,000mAh bank
items.bestFor: Commuters and travelers who want one grab-and-go battery, especially iPhone 15 and newer owners
items.tip: Check that the box says A1685 and pick your colour in the variant list. When flying, keep it with you in the cabin, never in checked bags, and don't use it on board.

facts.v: Up to 30W via built-in USB-C cable

alt.name: UGREEN 10000mAh Magnetic Wireless Power Bank
alt.label: Budget pick
alt.note: About ₱1,100 from UGREEN Official Store. The listing photo shows 20W wired charging, 7.5W to 15W magnetic wireless charging and a free USB-C cable. The listing doesn't name a model code, and the title also mentions a 5,000mAh size, so make sure you select the 10,000mAh option.

items.label: Best value
items.name: Anker Zolo 30W GaN USB-C Charger (A2698)
items.verdict: A tiny, low-cost 30W charger that fast-charges both iPhones and Samsung phones and is designed to stay cool.
items.summary: Not every phone comes with a charger in the box anymore, so check yours first. If you need one, this pocket-size Anker Zolo is an easy choice. 30W covers full-speed charging on most phones, and it speaks both Apple's and Samsung's fast-charging standards. Anker also built in a temperature sensor, which is reassuring on hot Philippine afternoons.

reviewers.point: Covered the local launch: the Zolo 20W and 30W chargers have foldable plugs, a temperature sensor that Anker says keeps charging 13°C cooler than standard chargers, and a stacked design about 25% smaller. Launch prices were ₱395 for the 20W and ₱495 for the 30W.
Anker's spec page for A2698: one USB-C port, 30W max, PD 3.0 and PPS, 100–240V input, 49 g.

Engadget's 2026 iPhone guide and How-To Geek's list of cheap iPhone essentials both recommend a compact 30W Anker USB-C charger as the one to get. They name the Anker Nano 30W, a different model from this Zolo.

pros: 30W with PD and PPS covers iPhones, Samsung and most Android phones
Very small, with a foldable plug
cons: One port, so one device at a time
No independent lab test of this exact model found
items.bestFor: Anyone whose phone came without a charger, or who wants a small spare for the bag or office
items.tip: ₱395 is the listing's base price. Unbox PH reported launch prices of ₱395 for the 20W and ₱495 for the 30W, so select the 30W option (A2698) and expect to pay a bit more. It has a USB-C port only; if your phone came with a USB-A cable, add pick #3.

alt.name: UGREEN Nexode Mini 30W GaN Charger
alt.label: Also great
alt.note: About ₱350 from UGREEN Official Store. The listing covers 20W and 30W versions, so pick 30W for full-speed charging on most phones.

items.label: Best spare cable
items.name: Anker Zolo 240W Braided USB-C to USB-C Cable (A8060)
items.verdict: A tough, independently tested cable for under ₱300, and one of the most popular cables we found.
items.summary: A second good cable means one stays by the bed and one lives in your bag. This braided Anker Zolo cable is certified by the USB standards body (USB-IF) and passed an independent tester's high-power check. It's also the missing piece if your phone came with an older USB-A cable but your new charger or power bank only has USB-C.

reviewers.point: Independent test: USB-IF certified (the reviewer says that's unusual at this price), e-marker present, and it handled a 140W continuous load. The braid is soft and flexible rather than stiff. Overall grade B+.
Same reviewer's main con: data runs at USB 2.0 speed, so treat it as a charging cable, not a fast file-transfer cable.
General advice: cheap cables can charge slowly, overheat or stop working within months, so choose a certified cable that supports your phone's fast-charging standard.

pros: Independently tested: USB-IF certified, with an e-marker
Covers phones, tablets and most laptops
cons: No video output or screen mirroring
items.bestFor: A spare for the bag, car or power bank, or replacing a frayed cable
items.tip: Pick 0.9 m for a bag or power bank and 1.8 m for the bedside. The price shown is for the base variant. iPhone 14 and older use Lightning, so they need a USB-C to Lightning cable instead.

alt.name: UGREEN 100W USB-C to USB-C Cable with E-Marker
alt.label: Also great
alt.note: About ₱290 from UGREEN Official Store. Per the listing name it is rated 100W (20V/5A) with an e-marker, which is enough for phones, tablets and many laptops. Choose your length in the variant list.

items.label: Best for commuters
items.name: Soundcore R50i NC Noise-Cancelling Earbuds (A3959)
items.verdict: Real noise cancelling for the daily commute, at a budget price.
items.summary: Jeepney engines, bus horns and train announcements add up over a long commute. These Soundcore earbuds use active noise cancelling to turn that down. They last a full day with the case and cost about ₱1,300. A Philippine reviewer found the noise cancelling works best on steady rumble like traffic and engines, which is exactly the noise most of us deal with.

reviewers.point: Scored it 4.3 out of 5. The noise cancelling handles low rumble like traffic and engine hum well but doesn't block everything. Comfortable for hours of commuting. Clear vocals with strong, bass-heavy tuning.

After a week of use: effective at cutting indoor and traffic noise, comfortable enough to fall asleep in, and the case doubles as a phone stand. Cons: sound leaks at higher volume, transparency mode is only so-so, and the default tuning is bass-heavy (fixable with the app EQ).

Anker PH lists model A3959 with adaptive ANC up to 42dB, 10mm drivers, Bluetooth 5.4 and IP54. Battery is 10 hours per charge and 45 hours with the case with ANC off, or about 7 and 30 hours with ANC on. It carries an 18-month Soundcore warranty, and the sale price on anker.com.ph was ₱1,295.

pros: Real noise cancelling at a budget price
Long battery life with the case
Case doubles as a phone stand
cons: Bass-heavy out of the box (the app EQ helps)
items.bestFor: Commuters on jeeps, buses and trains who want quieter rides without spending much
items.tip: Expect shorter battery life with ANC on (about 7 hours per charge). If the bass feels heavy, use the soundcore app's EQ. Choose your colour in the variant list.

alt.name: Xiaomi Redmi Buds 6 Active
alt.label: Budget pick
alt.note: About ₱670 from Xiaomi Official Store Global. Per the listing name: Bluetooth 5.4, dual-mic call noise reduction (ENC), 30 hours with the case, IPX4 and a semi-in-ear fit. It has no active noise cancelling for music, so it's best for calls and casual listening.

items.label: Best for trips and video calls
items.name: Ulanzi MT-44 Extendable Phone Tripod and Selfie Stick
items.verdict: A light 3-in-1 stand, tripod and selfie stick that holds almost any phone.
items.summary: A tripod stand is the accessory you'll be glad you packed. Use it for video calls, cooking videos, live selling, or the barkada photo where nobody has to stay behind the camera. The Ulanzi MT-44 folds small, stands on a table or the floor, and doubles as a selfie stick. Its phone clamp hides inside the head, so there's no separate holder to lose.

reviewers.point: Light at 422 g, with six sections that extend from 32.5 cm to 149 cm, a 360° ball head and a spring-loaded phone holder hidden in the head. The legs lock securely and it is stable on flat surfaces.

Same review's cons: less stable when fully extended outdoors in wind, ABS plastic build, a small screw cover that falls off easily, and sections that can feel stiff. The clamp fits phones about 6–8 cm wide.
Ulanzi lists six sections, up to 146.5 cm (57.6 in), and a foldable hidden phone holder. It also works with small cameras and lights.

pros: Stand, tripod and selfie stick in one
Hidden phone clamp, plus a 1/4-inch screw for cameras and lights
Sold by an authorized Ulanzi reseller (per the listing photo)
cons: Wobbles at full height in wind
Plastic build, and no remote included
items.bestFor: Barkada trips, solo travelers, video calls, live selling and TikTok or Reels
items.tip: Measure your phone with its case on: the clamp fits about 6 to 8 cm wide. On windy days, keep it below full height, and use your phone's timer for group shots.

alt.name: Ulanzi MT-44 (JG Superstore listing)
alt.label: Lower price, more versions
alt.note: The same tripod for less, from a seller whose listing bundles three versions (MT-44, MT-44B and MT-44M). The lowest price is for the plain MT-44, so check the version name before checkout.
